purpose: Run the friction ablation using the actual material coefficient consumed by Newton VBD FEM-rigid contact, after identifying ShapeConfig.kf as a no-op for that formulation.

intermediate_mu_probe.interpretation: One diagnostic sample at mu=0.3 still inverts the cecum. It reduces inversion severity relative to the mu=0.6 baseline in this seed but does not pass. No monotonic or calibrated material conclusion follows from a single midpoint sample.

interpretation: With mu set to zero on both the particle and instrument-shape sides, all three seeds remain positive-volume through the 24-step horizon; the authored-mu baselines invert cecum on all three. Action arrays differ by at most 3.13e-6, so these are close matched runs but not bitwise identical-action ablations. Peak tissue speed rises from about 12 mm/s to 85-136 mm/s, and the contact wrench channel falls sharply. This exposes strong sensitivity to VBD's friction coefficient and force/deformation coupling, not a validated fix: frictionless organ contact is not realistic, the tissue-speed spike is concerning, no grasp occurs, and all task stages remain incomplete.
decision: Keep the authored material unchanged. Use this only as a diagnostic cause-separation result; calibrate mu against instrumented tissue or phantom data and repeat across seeds and tangential trajectories before changing material settings.
limits: One scene and one scripted DemoPolicy approach; three seeds are not held-out anatomy, policy, or task validation.
No force-displacement calibration, sensor validation, or tissue-speed acceptance threshold is available.
The zero-mu override changes the global soft-contact particle-side coefficient and both instrument-shape coefficients; it is a broad friction ablation.
The reported wrench is a solver-derived proxy, not a calibrated force measurement.
No appendectomy stage completed under either condition.
privacy: Tracked report contains aggregate metrics and local ignored-run references only. Source data, frames, credentials, and personal information remain local.
